title: Introduce tenant cost compactifier and quant mentor CLI
author: Jordan Patel
release_notes: Adds tenant-aware compact cost templates and a new Quant Mentor CLI to propose safe quantization and batching defaults; CLI supports dry-run/simulate and exports deterministic profiles for Dedicated and Private deployments; no customer-facing API changes.
description:
Context and motivation: Large tenants see wide variance in per-tenant unit economics driven by traffic shape, prompt lengths, and tail latency constraints. Our existing autotuners are powerful but heavy-weight and assume long-running background sampling. This PR introduces a light-weight 'tenant cost compactifier' that builds compact, deployable cost templates by sampling a short representative window and synthesizing conservative batch/cache/quant defaults. Paired with the 'quant-mentor' CLI, operators can simulate safe rollouts and get human-readable advice for quant profiles and batching shapes.

What this PR does (high level): 1) New compactifier service that ingests sampled request metadata and outputs a compact template (batch shapes, cache-presets, quant-tier recommendation, safety margins). 2) Quant Mentor CLI (bin/quant-mentor) with subcommands: profile, simulate, export. 'profile' generates a deterministic recommendation; 'simulate' runs a metric-level dry-run against historical traces; 'export' emits a profile artifact compatible with Dedicated/Private defaults. 3) Telemetry hooks to emit cost delta and latency delta estimates per-candidate profile. 4) End-to-end integration tests & unit coverage for heuristics.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc reviewed (ENG-5124) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration smoke tests - [x] Telemetry events (cost_delta_estimate, latency_delta_estimate) - [x] Backward-compatible profile export format - [x] CLI help and man page

Commits summary: 1) Add compactifier core + heuristics (heuristics/compactifier.py + sampling connectors) 2) Add quant-mentor CLI and simulation runner (cli/quant_mentor.py) 3) Integrate telemetry and cost model adapter (telemetry/cost_adapter.go) 4) Tests and small refactors to the profile serializer (profiles/serialize.go) 5) Docs and examples (docs/compactifier.md, examples/quant-mentor-demo.json)

Changed areas (high-level): - server/compactifier/* (new) - cli/quant_mentor.py (new) - telemetry/cost_adapter.go (mod) - profiles/serialize.go (mod) - tests/compactifier_test.py, tests/quantmentor_integration.sh - docs/compactifier.md, examples/quant-mentor-demo.json

Review conversation: Maya: "Nice incremental design — two high-level concerns: how do we avoid overfitting to a short sample window, and do we provide safe defaults for latency-sensitive routes?"
Jordan (author): "Compactifier emits a confidence score and enforces a conservative safety margin on batch size if the confidence < 0.7. By default latency-sensitive routes (route metadata ms95 < 200) are assigned latency-first templates. Comments added linking to the confidence heuristics code paths (heuristics/compactifier.py:estimate_confidence)."
Leo: "CLI UX is good; suggestion to add a --shadow flag that can run the profile in shadow mode in Dedicated for one hour."
Jordan: "Added --shadow-duration and a telemetry opt-in; documented in docs/compactifier.md. Shadow runs are gated by a tenant opt-in flag to avoid surprises."
Priya: "Please include a short migration note for Dedicated operators so they can import exported profiles."
Jordan: "Added docs/compactifier.md section 'Importing to Dedicated' and an examples/import.sh script."

CI summary: Unit tests: pass; Integration: initial flaky e2e (timeout in warmup) -> reproduced locally -> increased warmup timeout in tests -> rerun -> pass; Lint: pass; Benchmarks: microbenchmark shows 6-12% per-token cost reduction on sampled tenant traces in the lab harness. Full CI run green.

Merge details: Approved by Maya and Leo after two rounds of review. Merged via squash on 2025-08-27. Post-merge: rollout plan executed to staging; one tenant group opt-ed into shadow run and observed expected cost delta within predicted band.

Backward compatibility and impact: export format is backwards compatible; profiles that don't specify quant_tier will be interpreted as 'preserve existing'; migration doc included. There are no API surface changes for hosted API. The feature primarily affects Dedicated and Private deploy workflows and the operator CLI.

Followups planned: - ENG-5402: auto-schedule periodic re-sampling for compactifier - ENG-5420: add ML-based confidence estimator to replace heuristic score - PM-318: surface compactifier suggestions in Console Defaults UI

review_comments: Two rounds. Primary concerns: safety for latency-sensitive routes (addressed via confidence/safety margins), shadow run gating (added --shadow-duration and opt-in), import/migration docs (added). Final: approvals from Maya and Leo.
notes_for_ops: Staging rollout: deploy compactifier service and CLI to staging cluster, opt-in a single tenant using examples/import.sh; run quant-mentor simulate against a 24h trace and verify cost_delta_estimate < 15% before shadowing; to promote to prod, run shadow for 1-2 tenants for 48h and monitor token-level cost and 95th latency metrics.
